A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

Inspect whether the criterion’s “inside” threshold is too permissive for this image (for example, whether the frog is actually seated within the bowl rather than merely overlapping its opening in the 2D view), and make the placement test explicit and evidence-based without assuming the reference is ground truth. Preserve the distinction between complete, partial, absent, and unknown, and require the trace to cite the frog’s position relative to the bowl rim/interior before assigning a label. The one unknown trace is a transport/TLS failure, not negative visual evidence; handle it as unavailable evidence rather than changing the visual criterion. Repeated high-confidence yes traces are a reason to investigate criterion or aggregation ambiguity, not to force a partial answer.
